method: Independent read-only production source and generated-source review; no builds, binary execution, CI, remote actions or production edits performed by this review.
remaining_limitations: A genuine global-record integration run of the new allocator guard is still a separate required validation; this review does not declare it complete.
Generic dynamic/existing-block allocator callbacks, OOM callbacks and their contextual/aggregate stack bounds remain unproved.

The unrestricted OOM callback setter and raw diagnostic/Print paths are outside the checked allocator entrypoint closure. No selected first-core setter callsite was found; they remain explicit nonadmission barriers, not silently covered by this review.
No arbitrary C memory-corruption resistance is claimed. Writable pointers and general memory utilities are not made immutable by these entrypoint checks.
No hardware DMA stop, PM deadline, original shutdown timing, target kernel stack capacity, native Apple execution or GPU initialization proof is supplied.

resolved_findings.resolution: Public wrapper rejects global allocator identities and independently rejects main/paged/nonpaged static tracking identities, including NULL or non-global allocator aliases, before any write or list operation.

Only the source-local static original implementation initializes global tracking. Its three source-conditional calls remain in the genuine memory initializer after successful tracking-lock initialization and private allocator setup, before MemoryEnd publication. Public same-pair reentry always refuses; a public readiness claim cannot open that path.

Exact global allocator addresses select fixed static tracking addresses, with nonpaged selection following PORT_MEM_TRACK_USE_FENCEPOSTS; writable pTracking/pImpl fields do not select global runtime tracking.

Non-global reserved pTracking aliases refuse before allocation/free mutation or release callbacks. Public release also denies global allocator identities; the static unlink helper independently refuses reserved trackers. The original release wrapper does not dereference pImpl; arbitrary dynamic allocator callbacks remain outside the bounded proof.

Existing-block constructor rejects wraparound and any claimed range overlapping the retained portMemGlobals object before writing allocator fields. Genuine caller-owned block behavior remains original.
